A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of posterior contraction for sparse Bayesian neural networks. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical results and proofs, without original experiments, simulations or data analyses. Its function plots are mathematical illustrations; Appendix A's empirical-norm results are theoretical.

after.justification: v2 remains a theoretical paper. Neither its main text nor appendices report original empirical outcomes; the figures illustrate specified functions and compositional structures.

M1.justification: The network and prior families remain, but their specifications receive meaningful refinements. Example 3.5 changes the continuous prior's slab weight from 1/T to exp[-2 C_A(log n)^2] and revises its spike scale. Appendix A.2 replaces the ordinary sigmoid with a scaled sigmoid. These change the specified models without introducing a new inference framework.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets or test scenarios. Added discussion of images motivates the theory and does not establish additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods experimentally. Table 1 compares theoretical literature; its revision does not add or remove evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to theoretical network constructions, classification risk and norm inequalities belong to the model and theory assessments.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests or empirical case studies. The additive, multiplicative, rotated and piecewise mathematical examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Revised probability bounds are theoretical derivations, not changes in empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added, removed or updated. The illustrative functions and principal contraction-rate orders remain the same; corrections to mathematical bounds and definitions are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Assumption (C3) now requires exponentially smaller tail mass in (log n)^2 and uses a smaller threshold. v2 C.12 replaces v1 C.10's binomial-tail argument, while C.13 adds missing weight-tail control and an explicit adaptive-shrinkage argument. Lemma B.4 revises approximation tolerance, depth and sparsity, supported by an expanded rescaling construction. Appendix A also corrects excess classification risk by subtracting Bayes risk and changes the empirical-norm upper-bound coefficient from 1/2 to 3/2. These substantially revise the mathematical support.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain near-minimax contraction and adaptation over anisotropic and composite Besov spaces. v2 makes the composite-Besov novelty more explicit, but v1's Table 1 footnote already distinguished earlier composite Hölder results. No new principal contribution is introduced.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds practical guidance favoring sparse architectures and sparsity-inducing priors, and explicitly extends the interpretation toward neural-network performance more broadly. Appendix A.2 explains why the scaled sigmoid accompanies unit-bounded functions. The existing computational and horseshoe-prior limitations remain.

D1.justification: The explicit prior hyperparameter recipe and approximating-network specifications are revised. v2 additionally details layerwise rescaling coefficients in C.5 and the exact network parameter count in C.8. These concern the theoretical construction; no implementation, hardware, runtime or code/data release is introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds Donoho–Johnstone (1995), Pope et al. (2021), and four references on CNN and transformer theory. Section 1.1 clarifies that Egels and Castillo's composite results concern Hölder classes, resolving misleading v1 prose while retaining its earlier table-footnote distinction. Publication updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: The main organization remains. v2 polishes prose, expands motivation and discussion, adds acknowledgments and proof pointers, and consolidates selected appendix statements. The heavy-tail proof moves from v1 C.16 to v2 C.9, and classification inequalities are integrated into surrounding text or proofs.

P2.justification: Table 1 is reorganized into single-function and composite-function columns, and a new Table 2 summarizes assumptions and theorems. Figure 1 adds panel labels and color scales; Figure 2 gains color styling. These revise existing displays and add a summary without changing the overall layout substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the paper's mathematical support by correcting the shrinkage tail-bound argument, supplying missing adaptive sieve control, expanding the bounded-weight approximation construction, and repairing the classification-risk definition. These address central deficiencies in a theoretical paper. The stronger shrinkage assumption narrows applicability, and new Table 2 incorrectly associates Theorem 3.14(i)/(ii) with prior families rather than assumptions (A4)/(A5). Those limitations do not outweigh the substantial proof corrections.
